_meta.purpose: validation fixture for Conestruct flagger-controlled alternating one-way traffic on a 2-lane undivided road (basic single work zone, one flagger station per approach)
_meta.structural_note: MUTCD TA-10 is the controlling federal typical. CDOT S-630-1 has NO general (non-curve, non-pilot-car) 2-lane flagger typical: Case 17 (sheet 9) is the curve-specialized variant, Case 42 (sheet 25) is the pilot-car variant. CDOT-supplement values (A/B/C distances, device spacing, fines-zone bracketing, work-zone speed assemblies) are layered onto the MUTCD core here and cross-referenced to the sibling fixtures.

ta10_basic.title: Lane Closure on a Two-Lane Road Using Flaggers (TA-10) - basic, one flagger per approach

scenario.posted_speed_mph: speed-generic (letter-coded A/B/C distances; CDOT key resolves by road type)
scenario.closure_type: lane (right/work-side lane closed; alternating one-way traffic in the remaining lane)
scenario.control: one flagger at each end of the one-lane section

advance_warning_sequence_per_direction.label: ROAD WORK XX FT
advance_warning_sequence_per_direction.mutcd_note: Note 3: ROAD WORK AHEAD and END ROAD WORK signs may be omitted for short-duration operations

advance_warning_sequence_per_direction.label: ONE LANE ROAD XX FT
advance_warning_sequence_per_direction.mutcd_note: B-position sign in the TA-10 diagram. This is the sign the audit finding B-11 concerns: the diagram shows W20-4, not W3-4.

optional_additions.label: BE PREPARED TO STOP
optional_additions.mutcd_basis: Notes for Figure 6P-10, note 4: 'A BE PREPARED TO STOP sign may be added to the sign series.' Note 8 (Guidance): 'When used, the BE PREPARED TO STOP sign should be located between the Flagger sign and the ONE LANE ROAD sign.'
optional_additions.interpretation: W3-4 is an optional FOURTH sign inserted between W20-4 (B) and W20-7 (A). It does not replace W20-4. CDOT Case 42 includes it (marked with the optional-device triangle).

optional_additions.label: END ROAD WORK
optional_additions.optionality: labeled '(optional)' on the figure, one per direction past the departure end
optional_additions.mutcd_note: may be omitted for short-duration operations (note 3)

flagger_station.position: 50 to 100 ft upstream (approach side) of the one-lane, two-way taper start, on the closed-lane side
flagger_station.source: Figure 6P-10 dimension between the flagger symbol and the first channelizing device of the taper (vision-read at 400 dpi)
flagger_station.night_standard: Notes note 7 (Standard): 'At night, flagger stations shall be illuminated, except in emergencies.' CDOT Sheet 2 note 22 details the flood-light requirements (500 W min quartz, 8 ft min height, no glare, illuminates station + escape path).
flagger_station.single_flagger_option: Notes note 2: low-volume, short TTC zones on straight roadways may use a single flagger visible to both directions (deferred; see match_rules)

taper.source: MUTCD Sect. 6B.08 para 14 (Guidance): 'A taper having a minimum length of 50 feet and a maximum length of 100 feet with channelizing devices at approximately 20-foot spacing should be used to guide traffic into the one-lane section'; example in Figure 6B-3
taper.explicitly_not: NOT the merging taper L = W x S. The full-L merging taper applies to lane closures where traffic merges into an adjacent same-direction lane; here opposing traffic alternates through the one-lane section under flagger control. CDOT Case 17 carries the warning 'THIS TAPER MUST BE SHORT ENOUGH TO NOT BE MISTAKEN FOR A TRANSITION.'
taper.downstream_taper: 50-100 ft with devices at ~20 ft spacing (Sect. 6B.08 para 12), guiding traffic back into the original lane

opposing_end.mutcd_device_run_out: the figure's far-end '50 to 100 ft' dimension spans from the work-space end to the end of the channelizing-device run guiding traffic back to the original lane (anchor ticks read at 450 dpi). It does NOT dimension the opposing flagger position.
opposing_end.cdot_opposing_flagger_standoff: CDOT Case 17 dimensions the opposing flagger '200' TO 300'' from the work-area end; Case 42 carries the same value annotated '200'-300' BUFFER PILOT TURNAROUND'. CDOT supplements MUTCD here - the opposing flagger stands 200-300 ft clear of the work area.

buffer_space.mutcd: no dimensioned buffer in Figure 6P-10. Notes note 6 (Guidance): 'The buffer space should be extended so that the two-way traffic taper is placed before a horizontal (or crest vertical) curve to provide adequate sight distance for the flagger and a queue of stopped vehicles.'
buffer_space.cdot: S-630-1 Sheet 2 General Note 24 (verbatim): 'BUFFER SPACE IS OPTIONAL. NEED MUST BE DETERMINED ON A PROJECT OR SITE SPECIFIC BASIS AS DIRECTED BY THE ENGINEER. WHEN A BUFFER SPACE IS USED, DIMENSIONS AND/OR DEVICES USED ARE TO BE INCORPORATED IN THE TRAFFIC CONTROL PLAN (TCP) OR THE CONTRACTOR'S METHOD OF HANDLING TRAFFIC (MHT).'
buffer_space.note: the S-630-1 Sheet 25 legend cross-references this as 'GENERAL NOTE 23' - stale reference; the note is numbered 24 in the current revision

channelizing_devices.in_taper_spacing: CDOT Sheet 2 note 18a: spacing in feet equals the numerical value of the speed limit (45 mph = 45 ft) for tapers and transitions - but the one-lane two-way taper carries the MUTCD ~20 ft guidance over its 50-100 ft length
channelizing_devices.tangent_spacing: CDOT Sheet 2 note 18b: along the buffer space or work area, spacing may not be greater than 2x the speed limit (50 mph = 100 ft max)
channelizing_devices.centerline_delineation: channelizing devices along the centerline boundary between the open lane and the work space (Figure 6P-10 and CDOT Case 42 both show devices along the work-space edge)

advance_signing_distances_cdot_key.source: S-630-1 Sheet 9 'KEY TO ADVANCE SIGNING DISTANCES' (also reproduced on Sheet 25)

cdot_overlay_signs.interpretation: CDOT's 2-lane flagger typicals (Cases 17 and 42) add regulatory signing the MUTCD TA-10 core does not show. See cdot_case17_curve.json / cdot_case42_pilot_car.json for the dimensioned sequences.
cdot_overlay_signs.fines_double_bracketing: R2-10 BEGIN DOUBLE FINES ZONE upstream / R2-11 END DOUBLE FINES ZONE downstream, star-marked (see Sheet 12 notes)
cdot_overlay_signs.work_zone_speed_assembly: G20-5P WORK ZONE + R2-1(XX) SPEED LIMIT XX upstream; R2-1(XX) restoration downstream diamond-marked (mandatory only when work-zone speed is reduced)
cdot_overlay_signs.sheet12_scope_finding: Sheet 12 'FINES DOUBLE SIGNING NOTES' are road-class-agnostic and list LANE CLOSURE among qualifying hazards; signs go where workers are present in the roadway/clear zone or hazards exist (notes 1-2). This is in tension with the Item 3 carve-out that set Fines Double applicable=False for flagger scenarios - surfaced in phase1_findings.md for triage.

operational_notes: MUTCD note 1: positive protection devices may be used per Sect. 6M.02

MUTCD note 5: AFADs (Sect. 6L.02) may be used where there is only one lane of approaching traffic in the direction controlled; CDOT Sheet 2 note 20: a flagger station comprises either a flagger or an AFAD
MUTCD notes 9-13: grade-crossing provisions (queue extension, flagger notification, left-side warning parity, railroad coordination) - out of V1 scope
MUTCD note 4: flashing warning lights and/or flags may call attention to the advance warning signs
